claims.text: The alloys under comparison are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets arise from variations in local lattice distortion.
Mechanical-property differences among these alloys arise from variations in chemical short-range order.
Local lattice distortion affects dislocation glide during deformation and failure.
Local lattice distortion affects deformation twinning.
Chemical short-range order affects dislocation glide during deformation and failure.
Chemical short-range order affects deformation twinning.
The quinary alloy has greater local lattice distortion than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quinary alloy has greater chemical short-range order than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quinary alloy will exhibit greater strength than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quinary alloy will exhibit greater ductility than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The predicted strength and ductility improvements are caused by increased local lattice distortion and chemical short-range order in the quinary alloy.
The comparison is restricted to equiatomic, single-phase FCC materials subjected to matched thermomechanical processing and uniaxial tensile loading.
A lack of significant differences in the proposed mediators and deformation mechanisms, together with no correlation with mechanical properties, would falsify the hypothesis.
